question: How are NYC crashes distributed across the days of the week, 2013 to 2025?

options.denominator: all 2,132,218 crashes with a valid crash_date in 2013–2025 inclusive; each crash row contributes one count
options.grouping: weekday of crash_date, Monday through Sunday
options.reason: A pooled count directly shows how the total set of crash records is distributed across weekdays.
options.answer: Across 2013–2025, Friday had the most police-reported crashes (338,800; 15.9% of in-period records) and Sunday the fewest (257,544; 12.1%).
options.interpretation: This answers the weekday distribution by pooling 2013–2025 inclusive: each row, representing one NYC police-reported motor vehicle crash, is counted once and grouped by the Monday-through-Sunday weekday of crash_date; Friday leads with 338,800 crashes (15.9%) and Sunday is lowest with 257,544 (12.1%). A pooled count is a direct description of how reported crash records are distributed over weekdays. It leaves unanswered how weekday crash risk compares after accounting for traffic exposure or how the distribution varies year by year. The data check found 0 missing or impossible crash dates and full calendar-date coverage in all 13 years; 136,969 dated records outside 2013–2025 are excluded by the period filter, and no in-period rows are dropped for missing dates.

options.metric: percentage of each year's police-reported crashes occurring on each weekday
options.denominator: all crashes with a valid crash_date in the same calendar year; each year's weekday percentages sum to 100%
options.grouping: calendar year and weekday of crash_date, Monday through Sunday
options.reason: Within-year percentages compare weekday composition across years without letting years with more crash records dominate the distribution.
options.answer: Friday accounted for the largest share of crashes in every year (15.3%–16.3%), while Sunday was the smallest share each year (11.5%–13.6%).
options.interpretation: This answers how the weekday composition varied across 2013–2025 inclusive by grouping each NYC police-reported motor vehicle crash row by its crash_date year and Monday-through-Sunday weekday, then dividing each weekday's count by all crash rows in that same year; Friday had the largest yearly share throughout (15.3%–16.3%) and Sunday the smallest (11.5%–13.6%). Within-year shares are defensible because they compare weekday composition without letting years with more crash records dominate. They leave unanswered the pooled number of crashes by weekday and any traffic-exposure-adjusted crash risk. The data check found 0 missing or impossible crash dates and full calendar-date coverage in all 13 years; 136,969 dated records outside 2013–2025 are excluded, while every in-period row is kept in its year's denominator.

answer:
Across 2013–2025, Friday had the most police-reported crashes (338,800; 15.9% of in-period records) and Sunday the fewest (257,544; 12.1%).
Within each year, Friday accounted for the largest share of crashes (15.3%–16.3%), while Sunday had the smallest share (11.5%–13.6%).
